amod:ablative-plating.name: Ablative Plating

amod:damage-resistant-coating.name: Damage Resistant Coating
amod:damage-resistant-coating.description: You dip the armor in a resilient coating, proffering unto it a higher level of resistance to a single damage type. amod:hardlight-joints.name: Hardlight Joints
amod:hardlight-joints.description: You replace the joints and other mobility-requisite parts of heavier armor (medium and heavy armor) with silent hardlight projectors. armor:ceramiron.name: Ceramiron
armor:ceramiron.description: Ceramiron is an upgrade to polycarbon armor, in that it consists of much the same pieces—several pieces of armor, including a vest, leg and arm guards, gauntlets and a light, visored helmet—but is made with a heavier material that is much better at deflecting bullets and withstanding the shock of impact. It's more than double the price, too, but it still doesn't quite break the bank.

armor:composite.name: Composite
armor:composite.description: Building on the concepts put forth by newtonium armor, composite armor aims to do the same but starting from a nanoprene base instead of a synthweave one. A skin-tight nanoprene suit is fitted with additional ceramiron plates to protect vital areas, and while it is still just as mobile as a standard suit of newtonium or nanoprene might be, the nanoprene base makes it just as loud as base nanoprene, making it more of a good option for people who need the protection more than they need the ability to skulk around.

armor:fullerene.name: Fullerene
armor:fullerene.description: Fullerene is one of the two major options for maximum protection available to people who primarily use heavy armor. Unlike composite armor, which is a little lighter but offers comparable protection (if you account for the fact that composite armor lets its user dodge more easily), fullerene offers full-body protection: an under-suit of nanoprene has supports and straps to allow the application of several plates made out of several different compound materials. While the armor is not incredibly heavy to use for most people, it still is restrictive enough that you get from it is what you get.

armor:leather.name: Leather
armor:leather.description: Everybody loves a nice leather jacket, and not just for the looks. Authentic leather jackets tend to offer a surprising amount of protection thanks to the durability of the leather itself, while still maintaining some level of mobility in them. Still, leather's a bit stiffer than most synthetic materials, which does mean that it hangs a bit heavier on the frame, even if it's not quite heavier than some alternatives.

armor:micromesh.name: Micromesh
armor:micromesh.description: Micromesh armor is a material that's exceedingly lightweight, if a bit noisy. The materials used to make micromesh tend to make crinkly noises when worn and offer the bare minimum protection possible.

armor:nanofilm.name: Nanofilm
armor:nanofilm.description: Nanofilm armor tends to be skin-tight and made of high-end materials. It offers the bare minimum protection, but it is quiet and form-fitting—and a lot cheaper than synthweave, even if it's a little heavier than micromesh.

armor:nanoprene.name: Nanoprene
armor:nanoprene.description: You'd think that with a name like nanoprene, which calls to mind a neoprene suit that's been enhanced with nanites, that nanoprene armor would be easy to move around in. And it is, for the most part: it's tighter and thus more restrictive than a full nanofilm or synthweave suit, but the problem is that nanoprene also just is a very squeaky, surprisingly heavy material. If you need protection at a good price, it does the job effectively, but for something that's just offering skin-tight protection, it is alarmingly useless in stealth situations.

armor:newtonium.name: Newtonium
armor:newtonium.description: Newtonium armor is manufactured by weaving together highly advanced polycarbon threads into a standard synthweave base, and then adding carefully placed newtonium-reinforced plates in key vital areas. The result is a little harder to hide under plainsclothes, perhaps, but it's surprisingly light for its weight class, very quiet, and offers great protection. It's also about as much money as a regular runner starts with—this kind of protection doesn't come cheap.

armor:plastinium.name: Plastinium
armor:plastinium.description: Plastinium armor basically consists of garments that have thin plates made of a compound of nanoplastics and aluminum which keep them somewhat flexible while offering just a bit more protection than slinging a leather jacket over your body. The benefit of it is that it's light enough as a result, but it is still more restrictive than light armor.

armor:polycarbon.description: Polycarbon armor is very apparent, but also very light. It consists of several pieces of armor, including a vest, leg and arm guards, gauntlets and a light, visored helmet, all usually in full black or with a bit of a carbon fiber look to it. It's the lightest of the options for heavy armor, but it's not easy to move around in at all. Great for cops on a budget, which if you're the NCPD, is you.

armor:polysteel.name: Polysteel
armor:polysteel.description: Polysteel is the other of the two major options for maximum protection available to people who primarily use heavy armor. The material is surprisingly light given the full coverage, which makes it very protective while not being much heavier than the alternatives—and it's got a hefty price tag to match.

Shields are used to intercept specific attacks, whether from close-ranged weaponry or projectiles such as arrows, by means of active blocks, as well as to provide passive protection by closing one or more lines of engagement during combat.

burners:tech-burner-l1.name: Tech Burner (L1)
burners:tech-burner-l1.description: A tech burner bears the words of a single tech, contained within as an encoded cipher. If the tech is on your class's tech list, you can read the burner and cast its tech without providing any material components. Otherwise, the burner is unintelligible. Casting the tech by reading the burner requires the burner's normal casting time. Once the tech is cast, the energy stored within the burner is expended, and the burner becomes inert. If the casting is interrupted, the burner is not lost.

gear:ammo-pouch.name: Ammo pouch
gear:ammo-pouch.description: A reinforced belt pouch for holding bullets and slingshot pellets. Easy to retrieve ammo out of in the middle of a fight. Can hold up to 50 bullets or pellets.

gear:antivenom.name: Antivenom
gear:antivenom.description: Sometimes colloquially called “antivenin” or “antitoxin,” a creature that drinks this small vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour. A creature under the effects of poison that drinks this liquid receives an immediate new save against the effect.

gear:armorers-tools.name: Armorer's Tools
gear:armorers-tools.description: This toolcase is used to build and repair armor. It include hammers, a fire starter, screwdrivers, tongs, charcoal, rags, and a whetstone. These tools allow you to work metal, heating it to alter its shape, repair damage, or work raw metal into useful items.

gear:arrows.name: Arrows (20)
gear:arrows.description: An arrow is a fin-stabilized projectile launched by a bow. A typical arrow usually consists of a long, stiff, straight shaft with a weighty (and usually sharp and pointed) arrowhead attached to the front end, multiple fin-like stabilizers called fletchings mounted near the rear, and a slot at the rear end called a nock for engaging the bowstring. This is a pack of 20 non-technical arrows.

gear:artists-supplies.name: Artist's Supplies
gear:artists-supplies.description: A canvas bag, pun intended, containing supplies necessary for the discipline of the visual arts. It contains brushes, inks, paints, pencils, drawing tablets, and other implements to create visual art.

gear:backpack.name: Backpack
gear:backpack.description: A convenient way to carry around gear. A backpack can hold up to 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of stuff. Can also be used to represent a suitcase, satchel, or really big purse.

gear:basic-toolkit.name: Basic Toolkit
gear:basic-toolkit.description: A small set of miniaturized tools useful for basic tinkering and minor repairs.

gear:bedroll.name: Bedroll
gear:bedroll.description: A zip-up sleeping bag that has a built-in air mattress and inflatable pillow. Not super comfortable, but better than sleeping on the ground.

gear:belt-pouch.name: Belt pouch
gear:belt-pouch.description: Used for storing small items in a convenient location for easy retrieval. Can also be a fanny pack.

gear:blanket.name: Blanket
gear:blanket.description: A typical blanket for keeping warm on cold nights.

gear:board-game-set.name: Board game set
gear:board-game-set.description: A board game set can encompass a wide variety of games that are specifically played on a board. This primarily includes games that have pieces that aren't interchangeable and have specific rules towards playing it. Real life variations would include games like Settlers of Catan or Monopoly.

gear:bong.name: Bong
gear:bong.description: A portable hookah for inhaling recreational smoke. This could also be a vape pen, a rechargeable mini-hookah that uses fluid tablets to produce smoke.

gear:builders-tools.name: Builder's Tools
gear:builders-tools.description: This rough, no-frills case contains hammers, drills, levels, stud finders, and similar heavy tools for construction and architecture.

gear:bullets-pistol.name: Bullets, pistol (20)
gear:bullets-pistol.description: A bullet is a kinetic projectile, a component of firearm ammunition that is shot from a gun barrel. These are primarily made of steel and lead. Pistol rounds are a lower caliber, usually, such as 9mm or .380. They also generally contain less powder. This is a pack of 20 non-technical bullets.

gear:bullets-rifle.name: Bullets, rifle (20)
gear:bullets-rifle.description: A bullet is a kinetic projectile, a component of firearm ammunition that is shot from a gun barrel. These are primarily made of steel and lead. Rifle rounds are a higher caliber, usually, such as the still-in-use 7.62x39mm (or 7.62mm Soviet), or the 5.56x45mm NATO round. They also generally contain more powder. This is a pack of 20 non-technical bullets.

gear:burner-phone.name: Burner phone
gear:burner-phone.description: The “dumb” version of a smartphone. It can do most of the things a smartphone can do, but worse. Its major advantage is not needing your personal information to work, and not being traceable to you.

gear:canteen.name: Canteen
gear:canteen.description: A half-gallon container for holding water or booze.

gear:chain.name: Chain (10 ft)
gear:chain.description: A length of metal chain. Useful for connecting heavy objects, chaining up enemies, or beating the shit out of people. The price is per 10ft of length.

gear:climbing-kit.name: Climbing kit
gear:climbing-kit.description: A climbing kit includes special pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness. You can use the climbing kit as an action to anchor yourself; when you do, you can't fall more than 25 feet from the point where you anchored yourself, and you can't climb more than 25 feet away from that point without undoing the anchor.

gear:component-pouch.name: Component pouch
gear:component-pouch.description: A component pouch is a small, watertight belt pouch that has compartments to hold all the material requirements and other special items you need to cast your techs, except for those components that have a specific cost (as indicated in a tech’s description).

gear:cooks-utensils.name: Cook's Utensils
gear:cooks-utensils.description: A knapsack containing spoons, measuring cups, pans, pots, small knives, and other items useful for the preparation of tasty, home-cooked food.

gear:corpo-pack.name: Corpo pack
gear:corpo-pack.description: This pack contains a suitcase, sleep mask, traveling blanket, lighter, tablet, a nice suit or dress, 2 days of mealbars, a canteen, and 2 doses of stimulant drugs.

gear:crowbar.name: Crowbar
gear:crowbar.description: Using a crowbar grants advantage to Strength checks where the crowbar’s leverage can be applied.

gear:cyberdeck.name: Cyberdeck
gear:cyberdeck.description: A compact but powerful personal computer. The typical cyberdeck looks like a black cube or rectangle about 6 to 12 inches in length. It can be accessed wirelessly by a user’s peripherals, but serious users utilize a physical connection to their datajack for improved speeds. Techwizards need a cyberdeck to store their tech programs.

gear:delvers-pack.name: Delver's pack
gear:delvers-pack.description: This pack contains a backpack, crowbar, hammer, climbing kit, flashlight, mess kit, 10 days of mealbars, canteen, water purifier and 50 feet of rope.

gear:dice-set.name: Dice set
gear:dice-set.description: A dice set is, well, a set of dice. They can be many different kinds: a full RPG set (including a d20, d12, 2 d10s for percentile, a d8, a d6 and a d4), a little collection of six d6s, or any variation you might like. Many different games can be played with a dice set: Liar's Dice, Yahtzee, etc. and a user proficient with this set is assumed to be proficient in them.

gear:diguise-kit.name: Disguise kit
gear:diguise-kit.description: This pouch of cosmetics, hair dye, and small props lets you create disguises that change your physical appearance.

gear:drugs-euphoric.name: Drugs, euphoric
gear:drugs-euphoric.description: Euphoric drugs induce a sense of happiness and connection to the world, granting advantage on Charisma checks and saving throws against fear, but disadvantage on Intelligence and Wisdom checks. The effects last 1 hour.

gear:drugs-relaxant.name: Drugs, relaxant
gear:drugs-relaxant.description: Relaxants make the user lethargic and sleepy, giving them advantage on saving throws against effects based on negative emotions (like fear and anger) but disadvantage on saving throws against sleep-based effects and concentration checks. A renegade under the effects of a relaxant cannot get hype. The effects last for 1 hour.

gear:drugs-stimulant.name: Drugs, stimulant
gear:drugs-stimulant.description: Stimulants make the user jumpy, nervous, and full of energy, granting advantage on initiative checks and saving throws against sleep-based effects, but disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saving throws against fear. The effects last 1 hour.

gear:edgerunners-pack.name: Edgerunner's pack
gear:edgerunners-pack.description: This pack contains a backpack, crowbar, hammer, three UV flares, two cans of spray paint, set of restraints, flashlight, 5 days of mealbars, canteen, water purifier and 50 feet of rope.

gear:electricians-tools.name: Electrician's Tools
gear:electricians-tools.description: A reinforced metal box containing voltmeters, wire snips, screwdrivers, pliers, soldering guns, circuit diagrams, and other tools used to work with electricity.

gear:executive-ring.name: Executive ring
gear:executive-ring.description: An expensive ring showing the wearer’s allegiance to a given corporation, typically given to middle managers and low-ranking corpos. Higher-ranked corpos have more expensive rings, typically with integrated electronics.

gear:eyedrops.name: Eyedrops
gear:eyedrops.description: As an action, you may apply eyedrops to your eyes. For the next 10 minutes after application, you do not suffer disadvantage on sight-based skill checks due to exhaustion (such as Wisdom (Perception) to spot something with your eyes, or an Intelligence check made with hacking tools to notice a change in some written code). A typical bottle of eyedrops has enough liquid for ten uses.

gear:first-aid-kit.name: First aid kit
gear:first-aid-kit.description: A small box containing bandages, sutures, ointments, and low-grade painkillers. Used to stabilize dying characters and perform minor medical procedures.

gear:flare.name: Flare
gear:flare.description: A flare is a single-use light source. It burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a lit flare and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

gear:flashlight.name: Flashlight
gear:flashlight.description: This hand-held light creates a cone of bright light for 60 feet and dim light for an additional 60 feet. A minute of cranking powers it for an hour.

gear:flask.name: Flask
gear:flask.description: A hip flask to hold a pint of hard liquor.

gear:footlocker.name: Footlocker
gear:footlocker.description: A small trunk that can hold 12 cubic feet or 300 pounds of gear. Needs a lock to actually be secure.

gear:grappling-hook.name: Grappling hook
gear:grappling-hook.description: A metal hook intended to be used with a length of rope. You throw the grappling hook up to catch onto a ledge, then climb the rope. Easy peasy.

gear:hackers-kit.name: Hacker's Kit
gear:hackers-kit.description: A palmtop computer, a variety of data sticks with anti-security programs, a black box VPN solution, and other electronic devices used to gain illicit access to private networks and encrypted data.

gear:hackers-pack.name: Hacker's pack
gear:hackers-pack.description: This pack contains a suitcase, tablet, cyberdeck, bottle of eyedrops, and 2 doses of stimulant drugs or relaxant drugs.
contents: 2 doses of stimulant drugs or relaxant drugs

gear:hammer.name: Hammer
gear:hammer.description: A simple tool with a weighted head for driving nails or breaking small objects. Can be used as an improvised baton.

gear:hobos-pack.name: Hobo's pack
gear:hobos-pack.description: This pack contains a backpack, bedroll, mess kit, lighter, flashlight, 10 days of mealbars, canteen, and either a tent or 50 feet of rope.
contents: either a tent or 50 feet of rope

gear:holoprojector.name: Holoprojector
gear:holoprojector.description: Most people just use these to watch holographic movies, but a shut-in can soup it up to act as a mobile projector for their avatar and use it as a tech focus.

gear:jewelers-tools.name: Jeweler's Tools
gear:jewelers-tools.description: A chic pouch containing tiny screwdrivers, chisels, hammers, pliers, lenses, and other items to make fine jewelry.

gear:ladder.name: Ladder
gear:ladder.description: This portable ladder folds up to a little over a foot long when not in use. Unfolded, it is 10 feet long.

gear:lantern.name: Lantern
gear:lantern.description: A rechargeable portable electric lamp. It casts bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. It lasts 6 hours on a full charge and takes about 10 minutes to fully recharge if plugged into a power outlet, or about an hour if left in direct sunlight.

gear:lighter.name: Lighter
gear:lighter.description: A rechargeable lighter to start small fires.

gear:lock-biometric.name: Lock, biometric
gear:lock-biometric.description: An electronic lock that is keyed to someone's biometric data. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with hacker's kits can pick this lock with a successful DC 19 Intelligence check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear:lock-keycard.name: Lock, keycard
gear:lock-keycard.description: An electronic lock keyed to open with keycards. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with hacker's kits can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Intellligence check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear:lock-mechanical.name: Lock, mechanical
gear:lock-mechanical.description: A mechanical lock that requires a physical key. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with locksmith’s tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear:lock-pick-resistant.name: Lock, pick-resistant
gear:lock-pick-resistant.description: A mechanical lock that requires two physical pick-resistant keys in tandem. Without one of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with locksmith’s tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 19 Dexterity check. Better locks are available at higher prices.

gear:lock-twofactor.name: Lock, twofactor
gear:lock-twofactor.description: A combination mechanical and electronic lock that is synced to both basic biometric data and a physical key. Without both of the normal ways of accessing the lock, a creature proficient with both hacker’s kits and locksmith's tools can pick this lock with both a successful DC 17 Intelligence check and a successful DC 17 Dexterity check, made within two rounds of each other.

gear:locksmiths-tools.name: Locksmith's Tools
gear:locksmiths-tools.description: This set of tools includes lockpicks, files, pliers, tiny screwdrivers, bypass clips, and other small implements useful for defeating physical and electronic security. These tools can also be used to disarm traps.

gear:mealbar.name: Mealbar
gear:mealbar.description: A single day’s worth of nutrition in a fairly flavorless emergency ration block. Unless you buy it from somewhere that actually makes tasty ones. Those might cost a little more.

gear:mechanics-tools.name: Mechanic's Tools
gear:mechanics-tools.description: This toolcase contains ratchets, wrenches, compression testers, ball bearings, lubricant, and other tools necessary to work on mechanical devices.

gear:mess-kit.name: Mess kit
gear:mess-kit.description: This metal box contains a cup and simple cutlery. The box clamps together, and one side can be used as a cooking pan and the other as a plate or shallow bowl. Useful for camping, living rough, or making meals on the go.

gear:microbrewing-kit.name: Microbrewing Kit
gear:microbrewing-kit.description: A case carrying bottles, stoppers, growlers, proof testers, yeast cultures, and items needed to brew booze from scratch.

gear:microlab.name: Microlab
gear:microlab.description: A small box containing a high-powered microscope, vials, chemicals, reagents, and other implements useful to create toxins, antitoxins, and targeted vaccines.

gear:mule.name: M.U.L.E.
gear:mule.description: The Mass Utility Labor Engine is a multi-legged robotic lockbox capable of carrying the spoils of any freelancer’s hoard while they are busy. The M.U.L.E. has a carrying capacity of 500 pounds and can follow simple directions, either verbally or by an app on the owner’s personal device. It cannot fight but will run if attacked.

gear:musical-instrument.name: Musical Instrument
gear:musical-instrument.description: These tools are used to produce music. Each category of musical instruments is its own proficiency. Some of the more common musical categories include: bowed string, electronic, keyboard, percussion, plucked string, vocal, and wind instruments.

gear:nightclubbers-pack.name: Nightclubber's pack
gear:nightclubbers-pack.description: This pack contains a satchel or big purse, overnight kit, disguise kit, two club outfits, flashlight, 5 days of mealbars, canteen, pepper spray, and 1 dose of a euphoric drug.

gear:pellets-slingshot.name: Pellets, slingshot (20)
gear:pellets-slingshot.description: A slingshot pellet is basically an oversized ball bearing that's been polished smooth and made of a relatively heavier material to ensure additional damage upon impact. They're still much lighter to carry than regular ammo, owing to the lack of cartridges or powder. This is a pack of 20 non-technical pellets.

gear:playing-cards.name: Playing cards
gear:playing-cards.description: A playing card set is a deck of playing cards. It can be many different kinds: a tarot deck, a standard 52-card deck, or more. Many different kinds of games can be played with these, and having proficiency with playing cards assumes one has skill in most, if not all, of those games.

gear:programmers-kit.name: Programmer's Kit
gear:programmers-kit.description: A small case containing microcontrollers, LCD screens, micro-sensors, cables, light strips, electronic reference manuals, and similar necessities for programming and reprogramming computer-controlled devices.

gear:quiver.name: Quiver
gear:quiver.description: A long tube to hold arrows. Can hold up to 20 arrows.

gear:restraints.name: Restraints
gear:restraints.description: These high-strength shackles can bind a Small or Medium creature. Escaping the restraints requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity check. Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of restraints comes with one key. Without the key, a creature proficient with locksmith’s tools can pick the restraints’ lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Restraints have 15 hit points.

gear:rope.name: Rope (50 ft)
gear:rope.description: Typically made of nylon or paracord, rope is useful for a lot of things. It has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check. The listed price is for a length of 50 feet of rope.

gear:salespersons-pack.name: Salesperson's pack
gear:salespersons-pack.description: This pack contains a suitcase, waterproof plastic zip-folder for documents, nice suit or dress, tablet, flashlight, disguise kit, shaving kit, perfume or cologne, and pepper spray.

gear:scammers-kit.name: Scammer's Kit
gear:scammers-kit.description: This small box contains a variety of papers, inks, seals, digital spoofers, and other supplies necessary to create convincing forgeries of physical documents and digital identification.

gear:shells-shotgun.name: Shells, shotgun (20)
gear:shells-shotgun.description: A shotgun shell, shotshell or simply shell is a type of rimmed, cylindrical cartridges used specifically in shotguns, and is typically loaded with numerous small, pellet-like spherical sub-projectiles called buckshot. A shell can sometimes also contain only a single large solid projectile known as a slug, fired usually through a rifled slug barrel. This is a pack of 20 non-technical shells, which can be either slugs or buckshot.

gear:shovel.name: Shovel
gear:shovel.description: Useful for digging holes or excavating collapsed tunnels in old ruins.

gear:smartphone.name: Smartphone
gear:smartphone.description: A typical consumer-model personal communication device. Can make calls, send texts, play games, and connect to the net. Also used for personal identification purposes and purchases if linked to your biometric data—and why wouldn’t you do that unless you have something to hide?

gear:smartwatch.name: Smartwatch
gear:smartwatch.description: A wrist timepiece that can also make calls and send texts. Typically linked to your biometric data the same way a smartphone would be. Can be paired with a smartphone to extend both devices' features.

gear:spray-paint.name: Spray paint (1 can)
gear:spray-paint.description: A can of aerosol paint used for street art or graffiti. Comes in a wide variety of colors.

gear:streaming-kit.name: Streaming kit
gear:streaming-kit.description: A personal array of recording devices that can wirelessly connect to the net in order to broadcast your activities to others. Typically includes a camera, microphone, halo light, and editing software.

gear:suitcase.name: Suitcase
gear:suitcase.description: A convenient, zippered container with wheels on the bottom. A suitcase can hold up to 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of stuff.

gear:tablet.name: Tablet
gear:tablet.description: A personal computing device with an 8- to 10-inch touchscreen. Used for reading, playing games, and watching videos more than for communication purposes, but can also send emails and make calls if it has an attached data plan.

gear:tailors-tools.name: Tailor's Tools
gear:tailors-tools.description: A well-kept container holding scissors, needles, thread, tape measures, body scanners, and other useful gear for making stylish clothes.

gear:tech-focus.name: Tech focus
gear:tech-focus.description: A special peripheral customized by a techcaster to connect all of their other peripherals together and make them work more efficiently.

gear:tent.name: Tent
gear:tent.description: A simple and portable shelter. Sleeps two people if they’re very friendly.

gear:trailblazers-kit.name: Trailblazer's Kit
gear:trailblazers-kit.description: A side bag containing a compass, a set of binoculars, a sextant, a global positioning unit, digital maps, and other tools useful for keeping track of your location.

gear:uv-lamp.name: UV lamp
gear:uv-lamp.description: A portable lamp that converts electricity into low-powered ultraviolet light. Suitable for growing a potted plant or recharging a solar-powered device (or person) in the absence of real sunlight. Basically, these are just annoying to Hacked and other creatures who are damaged by sunlight.

gear:vandals-pack.name: Vandal's pack
gear:vandals-pack.description: This pack contains a backpack, a bag of marbles or ball bearings, 10 feet of string, signal whistle, flashlight, crowbar, hammer, 5 flares, 1 incendiary grenade, 5 days of mealbars, lighter, 1 can of spray paint, canteen, and 50 feet of rope.
contents: a bag of marbles or ball bearings

gear:water-purifier.name: Water purifier
gear:water-purifier.description: This siphon and container allow you to turn 1 gallon of tainted or salt water into 1 gallon of drinkable water. It requires exposure to sunlight for 6 hours or being hooked into a portable battery for 1 hour. The filters need cleaning every 10 gallons or so.

gear:weaponsmiths-tools.name: Weaponsmith's Tools
gear:weaponsmiths-tools.description: This toolcase contains whetstone, tiny screwdrivers, extra springs, gun oil, files, wire brushes, and the necessities for making, repairing, and maintaining implements of death.

gear:wrist-nanobot-dispenser.name: Wrist nanobot dispenser
gear:wrist-nanobot-dispenser.description: Like a smartwatch on steroids. Useful for enforcers to direct their techs and control their special augments, but overkill for almost anyone else.

gizmo:anti-cloaking-emitter.name: Anti Cloaking Emitter
gizmo:anti-cloaking-emitter.description: While on, this device runs for 6 hours on 1 small battery, shedding bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Cloaked creatures and objects are visible as long as they are in the emitter's bright light. You can use an action to reduce the light, reducing the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius.
gizmo:anti-cloaking-emitter.effect: While on, this device runs for 6 hours on 1 small battery, shedding bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Cloaked creatures and objects are visible as long as they are in the emitter's bright light. You can use an action to reduce the light, reducing the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius.

gizmo:aqua-pack.name: Aqua Pack
gizmo:aqua-pack.description: This trendy little backpack, featuring a wave pattern design, expands into a nanotech cloak, which can easily cover your whole body. While wearing this cloak with its hood up, you can breathe underwater, and you have a swimming speed of 60 feet. Pulling the hood up or down requires an action.

gizmo:autocord.name: Autocord
gizmo:autocord.description: This 60-foot length of rubbery cord weighs 3 pounds and can hold up to 3,000 pounds. If you hold one end of the cord and use an action to speak the command word, the cord activates. As a bonus action, you can command the other end to move toward a destination you choose. That end moves 10 feet on your turn when you first command it and 10 feet on each of your turns until reaching its destination, up to its maximum length away, or until you tell it to stop. You can also tell the cord to fasten itself securely to an object or to unfasten itself, to knot or unknot itself, or to coil itself for carrying.

gizmo:ballistic-cloak.name: Ballistic Cloak
gizmo:ballistic-cloak.description: You gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws while you wear this cloak.
gizmo:ballistic-cloak.effect: You gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws while you wear this cloak.

gizmo:bubble-helmet.name: Bubble Helmet
gizmo:bubble-helmet.description: This item looks like a small disk of metal that sticks on the back of a wearer's neck. When the wearer submerges, a mental command causes it to unfurl a hyperglass helmet around the wearer's head. The disk recycles the wearer's exhalations and extracts oxygen from the water, ensuring a steady supply of breathable air. The helmet automatically retracts when the disc is not submerged.

gizmo:creepy-ass-theremin.name: Creepy Ass Theremin
gizmo:creepy-ass-theremin.description: You must be proficient with wind instruments or electronic instruments to use this theremin. They have 3 charges. You can use an action to play them and expend 1 charge to create an eerie, ooky-spooky sort of tune. Each creature within 30 feet of you that hears you play must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you for 1 minute. If you wish, all creatures in the area that aren't hostile toward you automatically succeed on the saving throw. A creature that fails the saving throw can repeat it at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on its saving throw is immune to the effect of this theremin for 24 hours. The theremin regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

gizmo:deceitful-masque.name: Deceitful Masque, +1, +2, or +3
gizmo:deceitful-masque.description: While wearing this masque, which comes in the style of any facial covering from goggles to scarfs, you gain a bonus to the saving throw DCs of your Nanophage features. You gain an identical bonus to tech attack rolls and the saving throw DCs of techs gained from the pretender class. The bonus is determined by the gizmo's rarity.

gizmo:discreet-neuroscanner.name: Discreet Neuroscanner
gizmo:discreet-neuroscanner.description: The medallion has 3 charges. While wearing it, you can use an action and expend 1 charge to cast the neurotap tech (save DC 13) from it. The medallion regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.
gizmo:discreet-neuroscanner.effect: The medallion has 3 charges. While wearing it, you can use an action and expend 1 charge to cast the neurotap tech (save DC 13) from it. The medallion regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

gizmo:encrypted-neuromanipulator.name: Encrypted Neuromanipulator
gizmo:encrypted-neuromanipulator.description: While wearing this headset, you can use an action to cast the neurotap tech (save DC 13) from it. As long as you maintain concentration on the tech, you can use a bonus action to mentally send a message to a creature you are focused on. It can reply, using a bonus action to do so while your focus on it continues.

gizmo:engrammatic-armory.name: Engrammatic Armory
gizmo:engrammatic-armory.description: This harness has three compartments, each of which connects to a miniature digital space that allows it to hold numerous items while never weighing more than 2 pounds.
gizmo:engrammatic-armory.effect: This harness has three compartments, each of which connects to a miniature digital space that allows it to hold numerous items while never weighing more than 2 pounds.

gizmo:engrammatic-cube.name: Engrammatic Cube
gizmo:engrammatic-cube.description: This metallic, yet flexible, cube contains a miniature digital space considerably larger than its outside dimensions, roughly 2 feet in diameter at the mouth and 4 feet deep. vehicle:dirt-bike.name: Dirt Bike
vehicle:dirt-bike.description: A dirtbike is a type of motorcycle designed for off-road travel across long stretches of land. With much of its frame stripped of protective materials found in your typical motorcycle in exchange for its unparalleled maneuverability across the land, it is the vehicle of choice for those that enjoy riding out of the city and across areas where the self-driving systems disengage.

vehicle:hoverbike.name: Hoverbike
vehicle:hoverbike.description: A hoverbike is basically a motorcycle-shaped hover vehicle with a wide base that has several hover generators mounted on the back: two in-line at the front to control the steering and manage weight, and two on the back aimed downwards at ~30" angles to stabilize, with a powerful propulsion engine mounted to provide forward motion. They are somewhat sturdy and a bit faster than a hovermoped, owing to the heavier engine.

vehicle:hovermoped.name: Hovermoped
vehicle:hovermoped.description: A hovermoped is basically a single-seated scooter with a wide base that has several hover generators mounted on the back: one on the front that controls the steering, and two on the back aimed downwards at ~30" angles to stabilize, with a small propulsion engine mounted there to give it motion. They are not particularly sturdy but can be quite evasive, reaching decently fast speeds despite being primarily built to be compact.

vehicle:motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
vehicle:motorcycle.description: A motorcycle, often called a motorbike, bike, cycle, or (if three-wheeled) trike, is a two- or three-wheeled motor vehicle. Motorcycle design varies greatly to suit a range of different purposes: long-distance travel, commuting, cruising, sport (including racing), and off-road riding, though this particular class of motorcycles primarily focuses on speed and agility.

vehicle:sedan.name: Sedan
vehicle:sedan.description: Sedans are the bread and butter of city traffic. If not a sedan, it's a van. Sedans are of the most commercially available vehicles to Neon City's residents and perform well during all times of the year before their warranties expire. Many sedans are designed for in-city use along the self-driving network.

vehicle:street-scooter.name: Street Scooter
vehicle:street-scooter.description: A street scooter—or a motor scooter, or just a scooter—is a motorcycle with an underbone or step-through frame, a seat, and a platform for the rider's feet, emphasizing comfort and fuel economy. Elements of scooter design were present in some of the earliest motorcycles, and motor scooters have been made since at least 1914 OW.

vmod:critical-shielding.name: Critical Shielding
vmod:critical-shielding.description: This piece of equipment adds a set of polycarbonate shielding around the more sensitive parts of the vehicle's hover engine or similar weak point. When the vehicle receives a critical hit, you ignore the automatic mishap suffered by the Weak Point feature of the vehicle, and instead destroy the Critical Shielding.

vmod:mounted-gun-port.description: This modification allows any vehicle that has a mechanism that offers cover to properly mount a gun, such that a gun can fire out of the gun port with relative safety, while still giving whoever is behind the cover an adequate amount of protection. weapon:automatic-rifle.description: An automatic rifle is a type of autoloading rifle that is capable of fully automatic fire. Automatic rifles are distinguished from semi-automatic rifles in their ability to fire more than one shot in succession once the trigger is pulled. Most automatic rifles are further subcategorized as battle rifles or assault rifles.

weapon:brass-knuckles.name: Brass knuckles
weapon:brass-knuckles.description: Brass knuckles are "fist-load weapons" used in hand-to-hand combat. They are usually pieces of metal shaped to fit around the knuckles. Despite their name, they are often made from other metals, plastics or carbon fibers. Designed to preserve and concentrate a punch's force by directing it toward a harder and smaller contact area, they result in increased tissue disruption, including an increased likelihood of fracturing the intended target's bones on impact. The extended and rounded palm grip also spreads the counter force across the attacker's palm, which would otherwise have been absorbed primarily by the attacker's fingers.

weapon:katana.name: Katana
weapon:katana.description: A katana is a Japanese sword characterized by a curved, single-edged blade with a circular or squared guard and long grip to accommodate two hands. Developed later than the tachi, it was used by samurai in feudal Japan and worn with the edge facing upward. Since the Muromachi period, many old tachi were cut from the root and shortened, and the blade at the root was crushed and converted into katana. The specific term for katana in Japan is uchigatana and the term katana often refers to single-edged swords from around the world.

weapon:knife.name: Knife

Originally made of wood, bone, and stone (such as flint and obsidian), over the centuries, in step with improvements in both metallurgy and manufacturing, knife blades have been made from copper, bronze, iron, steel, ceramic, and titanium. Most modern knives have either fixed or folding blades; blade patterns and styles vary by maker and country of origin.

weapon:polearm.name: Polearm
weapon:polearm.description: A polearm or pole weapon is a close combat weapon in which the main fighting part of the weapon is fitted to the end of a long shaft, typically of wood, thereby extending the user's effective range and striking power. Polearms are predominantly melee weapons, with a subclass of spear-like designs fit for both thrusting and throwing. Because many polearms were adapted from agricultural implements or other fairly abundant tools, and contained relatively little metal, they were cheap to make and readily available. When warfare would break out and the belligerents had a poorer class who could not pay for dedicated military weapons, leaders would often appropriate tools as cheap weapons. The cost of training was comparatively minimal, since these conscripted farmers had spent most of their lives using these "weapons" in the fields. This made polearms the favored weapon of peasant levies and peasant rebellions the world over.
